summary: Basketball on-ball defensive stance: feet wider than the shoulders and flat, knees bent, hips back, one hand low toward the ball, the other up at shoulder height.

environment.name: ball_handler
environment.text: Ball handler about 1.4 m in front at arm's length plus a step.

cameras.name: front
cameras.text: From the ball handler's view: a wide, low defender.

cameras.name: side
cameras.text: Profile: hips back, nose behind the toes, heels down.

cameras.name: low_wide
cameras.text: Low wide angle from the floor, court lines converging.

rules.why: feet wider than the shoulders (fastest response at about twice shoulder width)
knees bent 30-60 deg (knee angle 120-150 deg gave the fastest response)
back slightly forward, not bent at the waist
other hand at shoulder height to the passing lane

text.action: a basketball defender in a low on-ball defensive stance guarding a dribbler
text.core: Feet about 1.5-2 times shoulder width, flat on the floor and pointing forward; knees bent about 60 degrees, hips back behind the heels, back straight and tilted slightly forward, nose behind the toes; left hand low and forward toward the ball, palm up; right hand up at shoulder height, palm facing the passing lane; head up.
text.gaze: Eyes on the ball handler's midsection.
cues: wide base, weight on the balls of the feet with heels down
one hand low to the ball, one hand up to the passing lane
chest square to the ball handler
kinetic: sneakers squeaking, slight lateral motion blur at the feet
sweat on the forehead, intense focus
avoid: bending at the waist with straight legs
both arms straight out like a zombie

sources.cite: Stirn, Dolinar & Erculj 2016, IJPAS 16:53: stance width twice shoulder width and knee angle 120-150 deg gave the quickest response
FIBA WABC Level 1 manual 1.1.1: feet about shoulder-width, knees bent, back slightly forward, nose behind the toes
Breakthrough Basketball: stance slightly wider than shoulders, hips back, heels down
FIBA WABC 1.2.1: hand nearest the dribbler low, other hand at shoulder height
